description:
FILED s463f (Fable merge review of round 19, 2026-09-01), found attributing the re/subst.t companion mover.

SHAPE (probe scratchpad probes/tieref2.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs main 6e6f191):
    package FOO; sub TIESCALAR { bless ["x"] } sub FETCH { $_[0][0] }
    sub STORE { print ref($_[1]) || "none"; $_[0][0] = $_[1] }
    tie my $s, "FOO";
    $s = \1;        perl: STORE gets SCALAR   PCL: none  (FETCH then returns 1)
    my $v=5; $s = \$v;  perl: SCALAR         PCL: none
    $s = [1,2];     perl: ARRAY              PCL: none
    $s = {a=>1};    perl: HASH               PCL: none
    $s = \"lit";    perl: SCALAR             PCL: none
    my $r = \1; $s = $r;  perl: SCALAR      PCL: SCALAR  (RIGHT -- the value came through a variable)
    $s = \\1;       perl: REF                PCL: SCALAR  (second, minor divergence: ref-to-ref reports SCALAR)

So the DIRECT assignment of a reference-constructor expression to a tied scalar reaches STORE as the referent (or the constructor list) instead of the reference, while the same value through a variable is right.  Suspect the assignment emitter has a special arm for a `\`/`[..]`/`{..}` RHS (an alias-into-place or a construct-in-place shape) that bypasses the box-set tie dispatch, or box-set on a tie proxy unboxes one level too many when the RHS is a fresh ref box.  Discriminating measurement not taken (3 min): `./pl2cl` the two spellings `$s = \1` and `$s = $r` and diff the emitted forms -- if they differ at the p-setf head, it is the emitter; if identical, it is box-set.

HOW IT SURFACED: t/re/subst.t row 212 (`$tied_ref =~ s/non-utf8/utf8/ result`, the tied block at t/re/subst.t:838-886) PASSED on 12eacb5 only because the OLD s/// write clobbered the tie proxy with a plain string (the direct value-slot write #939/%p-write-match-target replaced), so the later `$s = \1` was an ordinary assignment.  With the tie preserved the STORE gets 1, `"$s"` is "1", s/..../ has nothing to match, and the row fails HONESTLY.  Rows 203/205/207/209/210/211 (fetch counts + the cow result) pass now.  Spliced into baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv 200/72 -> 205/67 with this cause.

BAR: the seven rows above vs perl (the REF case may be split off if it is a separate ref-kind fact); t/re/subst.t row 212 leaves the DIFF by measurement (205/67 -> 206/66 expected); Pl/t guard rows (tie-01.t or the file that holds the tie STORE tests) inverse-verified; a `cl/` change runs the full sweep, an emission change runs corpus-diff + emission-ab.

Region: assignment lowering / box-set tie dispatch -- NOT in either round-20 agent's ownership; pool it for round 21 (correctness slot).
subject: assigning a REFERENCE CONSTRUCTOR to a TIED scalar hands STORE the dereferenced VALUE -- `tie $s; $s = \1` stores 1, `$s = [1,2]` stores a flat list; via a variable it is right
